_note: THE TEMPLATE REGISTRY. One row per ALIAS SHAPE, never per mission.
A template says what a base quest can express and where its moving parts are. Everything in a
row was READ OFF THE RECORD with `gen_inspect qall <base>`, not inferred, and a row is only
added after its base has been read whole.
WHY THIS EXISTS RATHER THAN A C# FILE PER MISSION: a Delve is built from a shipped quest's SHAPE
(its shell: aliases, stages, place and marker slots), and a row says where each moving part is in
it. Both kinds, beats and board, run with NO driver: the stages are the state machine and the
objectives are shown by a fragment script gen_delve writes per Delve (since 2026-10-09). The two
kinds that chose a driver, two-beat-one-place and find-owner-or-buyer, were retired 2026-10-15.
TOKENS: a recipe writes <Place> and <Planet>. The generator maps them onto whatever this base
happens to call its aliases, so prose is portable across templates and an author never has to
know that one base says DungeonLocation and another says TargetLocation.

templates._shell: TRUE CONSTRUCTION (his ruling 2026-10-15): the build makes the quest with new from this file and never reads the base. Written once by `gen_delve shell beats` from the base above; ours from then on. The lint still reads the base (open).
templates._parts: Every alias the build takes off ANOTHER quest (remotePlaceFrom's request, vanilla's wave collection), written by `gen_delve shell beats` with the shell; with both, a build reads no quest (his 2026-10-15 'close the 2 places').
templates._playerAlias: MBRIR02Player, filled with the player as a unique actor: a recover beat's OnItemAdded hook sits on it.
templates._approachStage: A recipe's approach (civilians, losing the crate) fires here, before the first beat's 10. The base has no stage 5.
_shape: NO DRIVER: THE STAGES ARE THE STATE MACHINE (his ruling 2026-10-08, proven by gen_stageprobe).
A recipe lists beats by TYPE (use, pickup, deliver); each is a stock Default* alias hook that sets
the beat's stage after the previous step's, plus a few lines in ONE generated fragment script
(papyrus/gen/duo_qf_<id>.psc) bound to that stage. Consecutive use beats sharing a group are done
in any order behind one counted objective. The base's driver is REMOVED; the last step lands on
the base's completing stage 100, which carries the reward. See gen_delve_beats.cs.
templates._beatSlots: Beats 1 and 2 take the base's two marker+activator pairs; beat 3 on clones slot 1. Stages and objectives are numbered by the build from the recipe, not from this table.
templates._secondPlanet: Made ONLY when the second place is a request (place.second.remote), as the board's: a copy of targetPlanet (3) whose parent is FinalLocation (10), so <SecondPlanet> names where he flies. A found second place is on the main place's planet, so it has no planet of its own and the lint refuses the token there. Added 2026-10-14 for 10a, the first local-here, requested-there Delve.
templates._orbitFrom: place.third.orbit (2026-10-22, his 'go on 19a, try over') copies HIS satellite repair's orbit chain: TargetPlanetLocation (2, LocTypeOrbit, ALFG 20.589), SpaceCellRefs (10, LVLSC_AllSpacePOIs created at 2), SpawnMarker01 (12, from the cell by se_TravelMarkerLocRefB02) and SpaceMapMarker (16, from the cell by MapMarkerRefType, linked to the target by MapMarkerLinkedRefNameOverride so the star map names it; 896 of 903 space-cell quests in his load order carry one, his catch). Its parsec pick is replaced by IsInSameCurrentLocationAsAlias(the main place, LocTypeMajorOrbital): the orbit over the main place's planet, which no vanilla orbit alias does (measured 2026-10-22), so the first play is its proof.
templates._remotePlaceFrom: place.remote: true copies THIS quest's DungeonLocation (alias 0, a PCM_QuestGeneral request) over the base's, so the site is placed on another planet. Its alias layout matches the base's 0-5 (read 2026-10-14). One place only.
cannot: any order for pickups or delivers -- a group is use beats only

templates._shell: TRUE CONSTRUCTION, the board's (2026-10-15, his 'close the 2 places'): the build makes the quest with new from the shell and copies its borrowed aliases and wave collection from the parts, so it reads no quest. Both written by `gen_delve shell board`; ours from then on.
templates._questScript: THE MISSION BOARD TALKS TO ONE SCRIPT, vanilla's MissionQuestScript (Data/Scripts/Source): OnQuestStarted sets ReadyStage 5, the board's accept sets AcceptStage 10, MissionComplete() pays through MissionParent and sets CompleteStage 100, a turn-down sets FailStage 200. Vanilla attaches it BARE, with no driver, on MB_Bounty03_FCR02, MB_Bounty04_FCR04 and MB_Bounty05_UC (read 2026-10-14), and duo_MB28a_qst is that skeleton plus duo_bountyscript. So the driver goes and the base class goes on in its place, carrying the ten properties the driver set that MissionQuestScript declares; the driver's own six (GangMembers, Min/MaxGangMembers, targetNPC, EnemyType, artifactlist) go with it, the recipe naming its lists instead.
templates._borrow: MB28a has no player, no object slot and no second place, so the slate base's are copied in and renumbered (its 2 is MB28a's planet, its 11 MB28a's map marker): the player (32, unique actor Player; the arrival hook and a recover measure to him), its two marker+activator slots (1/2 -> 20/21 at the main place, 11/12 -> 23/24 at the second) and its second place (10 -> 22, FinalLocation). Every link inside is remapped, the slate's place 0 becoming 5; a link to anything else is refused. Read off the record 2026-10-14 (missionboard02a).
templates._itemSource: A pickup clones its item off the removed driver's CargoObject, and duo_bountyscript carries none: the slate base's cargo item instead.
templates._arrivalStage: His 2026-10-14: "You shouldn't recieve radio messages just after picking up a missionboard mission. It's a posting someone has made." So the broadcast plays on 15, set when he first comes within 250 m of step one's marker, armed only after the accept (10).
templates._entryStage: A board quest STARTS when the board refreshes, long before the player takes it, so nothing may spawn or show at stage 0: every step-one spawn, objective, counter and broadcast goes on AcceptStage 10, and the first step's hooks wait for it.
templates._allows: The fights from the first board build; use, pickup, deliver and talk since the borrowed slots (2026-10-14, missionboard02a). Not recover (untested here) and not choose (the board ends through MissionComplete, and a choice's endings complete the quest themselves).
templates._beatSlots: The borrowed slate slots, renumbered. Stages and objectives are numbered by the build from the recipe, not from this table.
templates._markerSource: PrimaryRef (alias 3): a ref alias filled from the place (ALLA from alias 5). It IS beat 1's marker, its ref type rewritten to the recipe's at, and later beats' markers are copies of it. Never removed: TargetSystemLocation and TargetPlanetLocation resolve FROM it (their system and parent aliases are 3), and MissionQuestScript.PrimaryRef names it. Its base DefaultAliasOnDeath (the driver's kill, no prereq) is removed: a marker never dies.
templates._driverAliases: EnemyType (alias 13, Optional, no fill): the removed driver's, named by nothing once it goes, so it goes too.
templates._second: The borrowed second place (22) is always a REQUEST on a board (the lint refuses a found one: nothing holds it near the first), guarded off the first site's planet. Its planet (25) is a copy of TargetPlanetLocation whose parent is 22, as vanilla MB_Cargo resolves its planets. A second request is proven (2026-10-14, duo_delve_twosite01a, two POIs on two planets); the guard is not yet played.
templates._place: The place is ALREADY a request (ALPS, PcmTypeKeyword none, with MB_IsPlayerLevelAppropriate and a habitability condition), dealt by the board in Overtime, so a recipe never sets place.remote: the lint measures it against the request pool as it does a remote place.
cannot: a recover or a choose -- see allows
a found second place (only a requested one) or a third place
an approach, a person at an ending
templates._who: A who BUILDS on a board since 2026-10-15 (duo_delve12a, his 'teach board who'): its stage numbered after arrivalStage (16 to 19, below the first beat's 20) and its distance hook armed only after entryStage, so nothing stands at a posting's site until the job is taken.
templates.verifiedFrom: gen_inspect qall duo_MB28a_qst and MB_Bounty05_UC, Defiant, 2026-10-14; MissionQuestScript.psc read whole

templates._kind: A Delve whose ONE place is an orbit (delve_space.cs). His 2026-10-22: "make a series of tests for remote and space alias sets. Idea being we learn in isolation how to build these sets", then "A" (teach gen_delve an orbit-only Delve). The ladder's harness first: graduate or remove is the exit condition in home-office office/spikes/2026-10-22-alias-set-ladders.md.
templates._base: One of his 62 remote-space quests, all of which carry ONE alias set (and MB01 the same ten): PlayerStarSystemLocation 0, TargetPlanetLocation 2 (by type LocTypeOrbit), the SpaceCellRefs collection 10 created at 2, SpawnMarker01 12 and PatrolMarker01 17 from 10, PrimaryRef 3 created at 12, SpaceMapMarker 16 from 10, TargetSystemLocation 8, the StartingQuestTargetOrbital collection 14 created at 8, StartingQuestTarget 15 from 14, PlayerShip 9. Read with gen_inspect qall, Defiant, 2026-10-22. Its own startquest did not start it (his, the same morning: 'I think it's expecting an event'); the shell keeps no event (ShellOf takes none), so a build is started by hand like every Delve. The base's GetEventData condition (UnusedConditions) is left out of the shell too.
templates._replacesDriver: The shipped mission's script (a Crimson ship, its gang). A test runs none.
templates._activatorFrom: The beats template's own activator (its alias 2 creates it), which carries no script. His MB01's duo_MB01a_act is NOT the source: it carries a script (the repair, which takes a kit and can spawn ships).
templates._beatSlots: The beat stands on the shell's own pair: SpawnMarker01 (12, from the cell by se_GeneralMarkerLocRef01) and PrimaryRef (3, created at 12, objective 10's target). Stage 100 completes the quest and carries the journal.
templates._tokens: <Place> is the orbit. No <System>: a rung may drop TargetSystemLocation, and a token naming a dropped alias is refused at build.
cannot: more than one beat, or any beat but use
a second or third place, a request, a theme, a who, speech
